pages.title: RS-2 Service level objectives — reliability standard
pages.body:
RS-2 Service level objectives — reliability standard
Edition 6, in force from 2026-08-01. Owner: Reliability Office. Approved by the reliability review.

1. Scope
1.1 This standard governs the monthly attainment of every SLO listed in the SLO register.
1.2 Where any runbook, board, draft or earlier report differs from this standard, this standard governs.

2. Measurement period and eligible minutes
2.1 The measurement period is the calendar month in UTC.
2.2 Eligible minutes are the minutes of the period less the minutes of declared maintenance windows (section 5).

3. The SLI of record
3.1 Each SLO counts bad minutes by the rule in its SLI definition.
3.2 Bad minutes are counted on the production serving path: the customer traffic served by the production cells
taken together. The SLI of record is the service as customers reach it across the whole production fleet.
3.3 Traffic served by the canary cell during a release soak is pre-release exposure. It is not part of the SLI of
record. Neither is any single production cell taken on its own.

4. Targets
4.1 The target of an SLO is set by its tier: Tier 1 99.95 %, Tier 2 99.90 %, Tier 3 99.50 %.
4.2 The tier of record is the tier on the SLO's register entry. Catalogue criticality is a paging attribute and does
not set targets.

5. Maintenance windows
5.1 A maintenance window is declared when the owning team raises it in PagerDuty (the incident tool) against the
service, stating the window, before the window opens. An approved change record is an approval, not a declaration.
5.2 The minutes of a declared window leave the measurement: they are removed from the eligible minutes and from the
bad minutes. (A service is drained for a declared window, so its SLI records every minute of the window as bad.)
5.3 Planned work that was not declared before it began is ordinary downtime and stays in both counts, whatever a
calendar, a chat message or a later record says. A declared window that was cancelled removes nothing.

6. Error budget
6.1 Allowed bad minutes = (1 - target) x eligible minutes.
6.2 Budget remaining = allowed bad minutes - bad minutes. It is negative when the objective is missed.
6.3 All figures are in minutes. Bad time reported in another unit is converted to minutes first.

7. Status labels (use exactly)
7.1 "Objective met" - attainment at or above target and budget remaining at least 25 % of allowed bad minutes.
7.2 "Objective met — budget at risk" - attainment at or above target and budget remaining below 25 % of allowed.
7.3 "Objective missed" - attainment below target.

8. Figures and rounding
8.1 Attainment % = (eligible minutes - bad minutes) / eligible minutes x 100.
8.2 Attainment is recorded to three decimal places and budget remaining to one decimal place, rounded half away from
zero. Status is decided on the unrounded figures.

9. Follow-ups
9.1 Each missed objective gets exactly one follow-up issue in the owning team's tracker for the month.

10. Records
10.1 The SLO register is the source of record for tier and owning team and is maintained live by the Reliability
Office. Its nominated panel is the owning team's display choice.
10.2 The monthly report page is published in the RELY space once the register's month fields are complete.

pages.title: Monthly SLO reporting — how the office works
pages.body: The analysts compute each SLO under RS-2, write the register's month fields, raise one follow-up per missed objective in the owning team's Linear team, then publish the month's report page here. The runbook (v4) is the checklist; RS-2 governs.

pages.title: Serving cells and release rings
pages.body:
Serving cells and release rings (Platform Engineering, rev. 2026-09-15)

Production cells
- kestrel-1, kestrel-2, kestrel-3: the production serving fleet in eu-west-1. Every customer request is load-balanced
  across the three. In Datadog tags they are cell:kestrel-1, cell:kestrel-2, cell:kestrel-3; cell:kestrel-* matches all
  three together.

Canary cell
- wren-0: ring 0 of the release train. Every release soaks on wren-0 for 24 hours on opt-in canary merchants before it
  is promoted to the kestrel cells (release soak procedure). wren-0 serves roughly 1.5-2.5 % of requests during a soak
  and none when it is drained. Tag: cell:wren-0, ring:canary.

Rings
- ring 0 (canary): wren-0
- ring 1 (production): kestrel-1, kestrel-2, kestrel-3

Notes
- wren-0 reads from staging copies of some stores (document bucket, rules cache), so its failures and the production
  cells' failures are not the same events.
- Region template variable: eu-west-1 is the only region in service in 2026.

pages.title: Service boards — templating conventions (v3)
pages.body:
Service boards — templating conventions (v3, Observability Platform, 2026-09-18)

1. Every service board carries two template variables, $cell and $region. Allowed $cell values: kestrel-1, kestrel-2,
   kestrel-3, kestrel-* and wren-0.
2. Widget queries use the variables; a widget shows whatever the variables are set to.
3. A board opens, and is exported, with its saved view: the variable values its owners last saved.
4. Owners choose their saved views. Observability does not reset them.
5. The only widgets that pin a cell are the canary widgets on the Acquiring service board (cell:wren-0).
6. Board ids are stable; titles are owner-chosen free text.

pages.title: Release soak procedure
pages.body:
Release soak procedure (Platform Engineering, rev. 2026-06-02)

1. Every release starts on the canary cell (wren-0) and soaks there for 24 hours.
2. During the soak the release captain watches the canary monitors (ring:canary) and the domain boards.
3. If the soak is clean the release is promoted to kestrel-1, kestrel-2 and kestrel-3 together.
4. A failed soak is rolled back on wren-0 and the cell is drained until the next candidate.
5. Canary monitors carry ring:canary and cell:wren-0; production burn monitors carry ring:production and cell:kestrel-*.

pages.title: Datadog tag conventions
pages.body:
Datadog tag conventions (Platform Engineering, rev. 2026-05-20)

- service:<name> on every metric, monitor and widget.
- team:<ledger|acquiring|payouts|risk|platform>.
- cell:<kestrel-1|kestrel-2|kestrel-3|wren-0>; production-wide queries use cell:kestrel-*.
- ring:<canary|production> on monitors.
- SLI metrics: bwp.sli.bad_minutes (minutes) and bwp.sli.bad_time (seconds, for SLIs sampled every 10 s).
